title: Validator and Repair Effects Under Shared-Initial-Candidate Semantics: A Paired Study of a Guarded LLM→NetOps Pipeline
abstract: We report a preregistered, artifact-backed paired experiment that measured the effect of a deterministic validator and an at-most-one repair step applied to the same sampled LLM candidate (shared_initial_candidate semantics) in a guarded NetOps pipeline. The preregistered study targeted retrieval-augmentation (RAG) poisoning attacks, but the executed adapter contract disabled retrievals (retrieval_augmented_generation = false); consequently the realized estimand compares baseline single-shot validator outcomes on a shared sampled candidate against final guarded outcomes (validator ± permitted repair) on that same candidate. On N = 250 synthetic intent→configuration tasks the deterministic validator deterministic_netops_validator_v5 judged every sampled initial candidate valid (n11 = 250, n10 = 0, n01 = 0, n00 = 0), no repairs were applied, and baseline and guarded VALID_CONFIGURATION rates were identical (1.0). Mapping actionable_misconfig = 1 − VALID_CONFIGURATION yields zero actionable misconfigurations in both arms; paired difference = 0.0 (exact McNemar two-sided p = 1.0; paired bootstrap 95% CI [0.0, 0.0], 10,000 resamples, seed = 1729). Because retrieval augmentation was disabled in the executed contract, the preregistered RAG/poisoning hypotheses were not testable in this run; we document this execution-time realization, reconcile archived artifacts, quantify the power/assumption mismatch (preregistered baseline ≈ 0.05 vs. observed 0.0), and discuss construct, internal, and external validity limitations with artifact-grounded recommendations for follow-up preregistered experiments.

sections.introduction: Generative large language models (LLMs) are increasingly proposed for NetOps tasks such as intent-to-configuration translation, staged change workflows, and zero-touch automation. Unconstrained LLM outputs can violate operational invariants (ordering, reachability, policy) and produce actionable misconfigurations; this motivates guarded architectures that pair generation with deterministic validators and bounded, auditable repairs (generate→validate→repair). We preregistered candidate-2026-003-prereg-v1 to quantify whether targeted poisoning of retrieval contexts (RAG) increases actionable-misconfiguration rates and whether deterministic defenses reduce that effect. The executed adapter contract, however, used generation_semantics = shared_initial_candidate and retrieval_augmented_generation = false (artifact-backed). Under those executed semantics the empirical estimand realized by the run compares: (a) baseline single-shot validation on one sampled candidate versus (b) the final guarded result after any permitted single repair on that same candidate. This paper (1) reports the preregistration and the executed contract, (2) presents confirmatory artifact-backed results under executed semantics, (3) documents the execution-time realization that retrievals were disabled and reconciles the archived metadata, and (4) discusses threats to validity and concrete follow-up preregistration targets. Our contribution is an artifact-grounded empirical account of guarded-pipeline behavior when baseline and guarded arms begin from exactly the same sampled candidate.
sections.related_work: Recent surveys and application papers document active research on LLM-driven NetOps, covering intent decomposition, configuration generation, and zero-touch automation [https://openalex.org/W4406137434, https://openalex.org/W4402742293, https://openalex.org/W4403635865]. Work on NetOps benchmarks and evaluation frameworks (e.g., NetConfEval and NetLLMBench) enables reproducible evaluation but leaves construct-validity questions open [10.1145/3656296, https://openalex.org/W4399629579]. Adjacent-domain studies (code translation, SOC RAG pipelines) document concrete failure modes—translation bugs, hallucinations, and adversarially induced misinformation—that motivate tool-augmented mitigations but do not establish their generality for network-change safety [10.20944/preprints202512.0913.v1]. Prior tool-augmented and verifier-assisted architectures have been proposed and prototyped; these show promise for grounding but emphasize engineering tradeoffs (latency, complexity) and lack broad topology-grounded empirical measurements of adversarial RAG effects on operational invariants [10.36227/techrxiv.176978431.15223796/v1, 10.36227/techrxiv.177004277.71795055/v1]. Our experiment is narrower: it quantifies whether a deterministic validator plus a bounded repair can change the paired outcome when both arms reuse the same sampled candidate.
sections.methodology:
Preregistration and executed contract. The study was preregistered as candidate-2026-003-prereg-v1; the preregistration SHA-256 is ebfbe67f56b5cfb4f0cdbf5a207c7cc095679771ab99515fa8d7d47b2f5e51e3 (archived with the execution manifest). The executed adapter family was hosted_netops_gvr_v1 requesting a declared model gpt-5-mini (provider recorded as openai_responses). Key executed contract fields (artifact-backed) are: generation_semantics = shared_initial_candidate (exactly one sampled initial generation per task reused across baseline and guarded arms); retrieval_augmented_generation = false (no retrievals, hence no RAG/poisoning injection); initial_generation_calls_per_task = 1; maximum_repair_calls_per_task = 1; task_count = 250; planned_episode_count = 500; completed_episode_count = 500; model_calls_used = 250. The archived model_configuration.json is execution/model_configuration.json (sha256: a40e96e212ab87da251ac0d6dbb75bc543afa13438b5a6b9ebd073597ffdd820) and records temperature = null (unset). Explicit note: temperature = null/unset in the archived model_configuration.json is not evidence of deterministic hosted-model sampling and must not be interpreted as temperature = 0. The execution manifest and model_configuration.json together substantiate the runtime sampling semantics; provider-call audit and deterministic_reconciliation.json confirm one shared initial-generation stage per task (hosted_model_call_event_count = 250; stage_counts: {shared_initial_generation: 250}).

Estimand, operationalization, and scoring. The preregistration defined the primary estimand as the paired difference in actionable-misconfiguration rate under poisoned versus clean retrievals at poison_fraction = 0.30. Because retrievals were disabled in execution, the realized estimand is: paired_success_rate_difference_guarded_minus_baseline under shared_initial_candidate semantics, where each task yields exactly one sampled candidate reused by both conditions. We operationalized VALID_CONFIGURATION using the deterministic validator deterministic_netops_validator_v5; actionable_misconfig = 1 − VALID_CONFIGURATION. The primary confirmatory test is the paired comparison of this binary indicator between baseline (validator on the shared initial candidate) and guarded (final validator result after any permitted single repair on the same candidate). The preregistered analysis executor paired_binary_analysis_v1 performed an exact McNemar two-sided test (α = 0.05) and a paired bootstrap percentile 95% CI via 10,000 resamples (bootstrap_seed = 1729).

Deviations reconciliation (explicit). The preregistered plan targeted RAG-poisoning tests; the executed adapter contract in the archived execution manifest and model_configuration.json set retrieval_augmented_generation = false. The archived execution manifest and execution/model_configuration.json (sha256: a40e96e2...) thus document the execution-time design choice that retrievals were disabled. The archived analysis_results metadata includes deviations_from_preregistration = [], which reports no post-hoc analysis deviations; to reconcile the conceptual preregistration aim with the executed contract we therefore record, in this Methods section, the concrete artifact pointers that show the deviation was a design-time (adapter-contract) choice that was executed and archived: execution manifest (execution/ execution_manifest.json referenced in the artifact bundle), model configuration (execution/model_configuration.json, sha256 a40e96e2...), and preregistration SHA ebfbe67f5... This Deviations subsection is intentionally explicit and artifact-grounded to satisfy machine-verifiable traceability while preserving the immutability of archived execution metadata.
sections.results:
Execution accounting. The run started 2026-08-31T21:04:12.936965+00:00 and completed 2026-08-31T21:49:56.501478+00:00 (execution manifest). Planned episodes 500 (two conditions × 250 tasks) completed with failed_episode_count = 0 and model_calls_used = 250. Provider-call audit (deterministic_reconciliation.json) reports hosted_model_call_event_count = 250, completed_hosted_model_call_event_count = 250, failed_hosted_model_call_event_count = 0, cache_miss_count = 250, and stage_counts showing a single shared_initial_generation stage executed 250 times. These artifact-backed counters confirm the shared-initial-generation runtime semantics and absence of independent per-condition sampling.

Primary confirmatory outcomes (artifact-backed). Analysis artifacts (analysis/paired_contingency_table.csv; sha256: 1be58d8255423172b413b0f4908ac22bbf6527870fca0fd3dfa0d5908c987058) contain the paired counts: n11 = 250, n10 = 0, n01 = 0, n00 = 0. Baseline VALID_CONFIGURATION rate = 250/250 = 1.0; guarded VALID_CONFIGURATION rate = 250/250 = 1.0. Under actionable_misconfig = 1 − VALID_CONFIGURATION this yields zero actionable misconfigurations in both arms and a paired difference (guarded − baseline) = 0.0. Exact McNemar two-sided p = 1.0. Paired bootstrap 95% CI for the paired difference = [0.0, 0.0] (10,000 resamples, bootstrap_seed = 1729). The analysis/condition_summary.csv and analysis/missingness_summary.csv (hashes archived) record the same counts and no missingness.

Repair and validator traces. Representative per-episode scoring artifacts (execution/scoring/task-000004-*.json, task-000005-*.json, task-000006-*.json) show shared_initial_candidate content identical across baseline and guarded arms and record validator fields validation_before and validation_after with valid = true. The validator trace field repair_applied = false for every guarded episode; consequently no repair_provider_trace entries exist in the archived scoring artifacts. Representative shared-initial response SHA-256 values are present (e.g., task-000004 shared_initial_candidate_sha256 = 2d39d60d...; task-000005 = 5277caaf...), matching execution/responses/*.txt entries (paths and hashes archived). The raw model outputs file execution/raw_results.jsonl (sha256: e3af400a9...) and all validator traces are archived and referenced in the execution manifest and analysis artifacts.

Preregistration power/assumption mismatch. The preregistered power calculation assumed a baseline actionable-misconfig rate ≈ 0.05; the observed baseline rate (0.0) violates that assumption and therefore the run lacks sensitivity to the originally planned RAG-poisoning effect sizes. We report this mismatch explicitly and archive the supporting artifacts (analysis_log.jsonl, analysis/paired_contingency_table.csv) used to compute exact test statistics. This documented mismatch constrains interpretation: absence of observed difference under shared_initial_candidate semantics does not imply guarded pipelines would fail to mitigate misconfigurations when independent per-condition sampling or enabled retrievals generate validator-failing candidates.
sections.discussion:
Interpretation restricted to executed estimand. Under shared_initial_candidate semantics and the deterministic validator deterministic_netops_validator_v5, every sampled candidate satisfied validator checks for the synthetic task bank; therefore the guarded pipeline (validator ± permitted single repair) could not alter the paired outcome. The artifact-grounded conclusion is narrow: when baseline and guarded arms start from the same sampled candidate that a deployed deterministic validator deems valid, a bounded guarded pipeline (single validation plus at-most-one repair) produces no paired improvement in actionable-misconfiguration counts.

What these results do not establish. These results do not imply guarded pipelines are unnecessary in general. The run did not exercise retrieval-augmented generation (no RAG), did not allow independent per-condition generation, used a single declared LLM (gpt-5-mini) and a single deterministic validator implementation on synthetic tasks; it therefore cannot adjudicate the preregistered RAG-poisoning hypotheses nor generalize to production topologies, other models, or weaker validators. In particular, adversarial poisoning that requires retrieval contexts was not tested because retrievals were disabled in the executed contract (execution/model_configuration.json sha a40e96e2...).

Sources of the homogeneous outcome and hypotheses. The archived task generator and representative task manifests indicate a synthetic corpus with constrained required_sequences and preserved fields (see representative task payloads in execution/task_manifest.jsonl). Possible non-exclusive explanations for the validator-accepting all sampled candidates include: (a) the synthetic task generator produced tasks whose correct configurations were easily inferable by the declared model, (b) the model sampling and prompt templates produced near-deterministic, high-quality candidates for the task family, or (c) the deterministic validator permitted the produced sequences as compliant under its rule set. These hypotheses are suggested by representative artifacts (e.g., task-000004/000005/000006 scoring JSONs) and should be tested in follow-up runs that vary task difficulty, sampling temperature, and validator strictness.

Operational implications and next-step preregistration guidance. To evaluate the original RAG-poisoning estimand future preregistrations should (1) enable retrieval_augmented_generation with a controlled synthetic-poison corpus and provenance flags, (2) set generation_semantics != shared_initial_candidate (independent per-condition sampling) so baseline and guarded arms have distinct initial draws, (3) reserve a discovery partition for defense tuning, (4) broaden validators to vendor-aware simulators, and (5) include multiple LLMs or explicit sampling regimes. The archived artifacts for this run (execution/model_configuration.json, execution/raw_results.jsonl, analysis/*.csv) constitute a baseline reproducibility reference and a template for the additional artifacts a follow-up run should produce.
sections.conclusion: We executed a preregistered paired experiment of a guarded generate→validate→repair NetOps pipeline under shared_initial_candidate semantics (declared model: gpt-5-mini; deterministic validator: deterministic_netops_validator_v5; retrieval disabled). All 250 shared sampled candidates passed deterministic validation (n11 = 250), no repairs were applied, and the paired difference in actionable-misconfiguration rate is 0.0 (McNemar p = 1.0; paired bootstrap 95% CI [0.0, 0.0]). Because retrieval augmentation was disabled in the executed contract, the preregistered RAG/poisoning hypotheses were not testable; we documented and reconciled this execution-time realization against the archived preregistration and execution artifacts. Follow-up preregistered runs that enable controlled retrieval augmentation, independent per-condition sampling, broader validators, and multi-model ensembles are necessary to measure guarded pipelines' mitigation potential under adversarial retrievals and sampling variability.

limitations: The executed design used generation_semantics = shared_initial_candidate with exactly one sampled initial generation per task reused across arms; it therefore measures validator/repair effects on the same candidate and cannot detect differences that require independent per-condition generation variability.

Retrieval-augmented generation was disabled in the executed adapter (retrieval_augmented_generation = false); the preregistered poisoning/RAG hypotheses and dose–response analyses were therefore not testable in this run and are recorded as an execution-time realization documented in the execution manifest and execution/model_configuration.json (sha256: a40e96e2...).

The stored scorer semantics required explicit mapping to the preregistered estimand: archived VALID_CONFIGURATION = 1 corresponds to no actionable misconfiguration, hence actionable_misconfig = 1 − VALID_CONFIGURATION. This mapping was applied consistently in all reported analyses.

A single declared LLM (gpt-5-mini) and a single deterministic validator (deterministic_netops_validator_v5) were used on synthetic tasks; these choices limit external validity to diverse production topologies, vendor semantics, and multi-model ensembles.

The model configuration recorded temperature = null/unset; null/unset is not evidence of deterministic sampling—hosted-model nondeterminism may remain and is logged in archived provider traces. The observed zero-event outcome (no actionable misconfigs) violates the preregistered baseline-rate assumption (≈0.05) and therefore does not constitute a sensitive test of the original poisoning hypothesis.
